A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaPert research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated, and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original K562 and RPE1 prediction experiments, component ablations, regularization sensitivity, and HIRA pathway analysis.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds evaluations on JURKAT and HEPG2, cross-cell-line transfer, graph and DEG-threshold analyses, and broader pathway experiments.

M1.justification: The perturbation-conditioned subgraph selection, context aggregation, and three-term training objective remain unchanged in Equations 5–21. v2 clarifies GPT-4o versus text-embedding roles and documents inference architecture; these disclosures do not establish a changed underlying method.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands from K562 and RPE1 to include JURKAT and HEPG2. Appendix C also introduces a distinct transfer scenario: training on RPE1, HEPG2, and JURKAT while holding out K562 as an unseen cellular context.

E2.justification: The original six main baselines remain, but v2 Tables 9–12 add Context Mean, Linear-GenePT, Linear-OneHot, scGPT, and Geneformer to the reported comparisons. The new cross-cell-line comparison also includes Perturb Mean, substantially broadening the controls beyond v1's comparator set.

E3.justification: v2 adds cross-cell-line testing, MAE-based evaluation, and the Systema protocol with perturbation/control references, top-20-gene scores, and centroid accuracy. Appendix A/Table 5 changes reported effect-size grouping from fixed DEG-percentage bins to within-dataset DEG-count tertiles. Appendix D additionally specifies and sweeps FDR/LFC thresholds. These are substantive reported protocol changes, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices D–G add DEG-definition sensitivity, graph-source and density ablations, fixed versus adaptive neighborhood comparisons, attention-threshold sensitivity, and DEG/non-DEG error analysis. Pathway validation expands to 272 K562 perturbations and pathway-specific rankings. The original loss/context ablations and HIRA case study are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies BH-adjusted Wilcoxon testing for DEG identification and 300 permutations for GSEA, extending statistical-procedure documentation. Existing mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged; neither version provides explicit training seed counts, and v2 does not establish an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–3 remain unchanged, but v2 adds extensive benchmark, transfer, Systema, ablation, and pathway results. For example, new Table 13 reports transfer Pearson correlation of 0.4601 for AdaPert, versus 0.5149 for Linear-GenePT and 0.6501 for Perturb Mean. Some appendix values differ from retained main results without reconciliation, such as K562 TxPert Pearson correlation of 0.5879 versus 0.580. v1 Table 10's RPE1 DES@100 and significant-gene Spearman entries are omitted.

T1.justification: The numbered mathematical formulation and metric equations, Equations 1–30, are retained. v2 adds empirical evaluation procedures but no new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that sparse perturbation-conditioned context and signal–noise separation mitigate mean collapse and improve DEG-aware prediction. v2 names the expanded benchmarks and highlights a 28% improvement already reported in v1 Table 3; the core contribution and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning graph coverage versus density, robustness to DEG definitions, and recovery of cell-specific pathways. It also identifies cross-cell-line limitations: simple mean and linear predictors can outperform AdaPert, with discussion of conserved perturbation effects and cell-state variation. These materially expand the mechanism explanations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 adds inference details including a four-layer GATv2 with concatenated skip connections, clarifies semantic embedding construction, and documents new graph and threshold settings. Conversely, it removes v1 Appendix E's training/model-selection description and Table 8's TxPert hyperparameter search space, including optimization budgets and validation-based selection information.

R1.justification: v2 adds application citations including Kim et al. (2024), Ishikawa et al. (2023), and Gonzalez et al. (2025), while removing Dunefsky et al. (2024) and Feng et al. (2024). The data-driven versus knowledge-driven taxonomy and positioning of AdaPert remain essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The appendices are substantially reorganized: baseline and metric descriptions are consolidated under Experiment Settings, related work moves from C to H, and pathway discussion is consolidated within expanded case studies. v2 adds an appendix contents list, rewrites the abstract and portions of the introduction/data exposition, and adds Impact Statement and Acknowledgments sections.

P2.justification: v2 adds an inference schematic, benchmark and Systema charts/tables, threshold heatmaps, graph comparisons, error boxplots, and pathway-ranking displays. Original distribution Figures 7–8 are combined into Figure 6, and the HIRA display is retained as Figure 28. Dataset tables are expanded and restructured, while the hyperparameter table is removed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the empirical foundation through simple mean/linear controls, fixed-neighborhood comparisons, DEG-threshold robustness tests, and pathway validation across 272 perturbations instead of relying on the HIRA example alone. The transfer study also exposes an important applicability limitation. These additions address significant gaps in v1's evidence for the proposed mechanism and biological utility. Removal of tuning details and unreconciled main/appendix results weaken reproducibility, but the broader, more diagnostic evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
